system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'

T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
LENA VARGA-HOLM
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
Halden Pay
Data Platform Hiring Team
Application: Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform
Dear Hiring Team,
Your emphasis on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines matches my approach to
data engineering: well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts and warehouses that analysts can
trust. With 9 years of experience building batch and streaming platforms, including
transaction reconciliation and finance data warehouses in payments, I bring directly relevant
experience to Halden Pay’s Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role.
At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own the ingestion layer spanning approximately 140 Airflow DAGs
into Snowflake. I migrated transformation logic from stored procedures to more than 420 dbt
models, with tests on every model, reducing nightly runtime from 5h10 to 1h35. By
introducing JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product teams and the data
team, I also helped reduce broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine per month to
two. These results reflect the combination of platform operation, performance improvement
and enforceable data quality standards your team needs.
At Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark reconciliation jobs processing approximately 1.2 TB daily on
AWS EMR, designed a Redshift star schema for finance and risk, and implemented Great
Expectations checks on critical finance tables. I also developed a reusable Python library for
S3 and Glue catalog access used by four teams. My cloud experience is in AWS rather than
Google Cloud, alongside Snowflake, Docker and GitHub Actions. This provides a relevant
foundation in cloud data platforms, while my Airflow, dbt, Python and SQL experience aligns
directly with your engineering stack.
Halden Pay’s stated values of Together and Ownership are reflected in how I work with
product teams on data contracts, mentor two engineers and run weekly platform office hours.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how this experience could support a reliable
shared platform for your analysts, data scientists and product teams. Thank you for
considering my application.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
